messages:
jason-support: FYI — we just got a Sev2 from AcmeCorp. They see normal TTFB on streaming but very high p99 total time (requests finishing ~10-20s). Non-streaming paths are unaffected. Customer reproduced 3x in last hour.

maria: Thanks. Can you paste the customer request headers + sample response? Any recent config changes to proxy/flush windows?

jason-support: Pasted anon headers below, they use SSE (client=browser) over h2 -> our edge -> runtime. No config changes from them. We did a small proxy TLS cert rotate earlier but shouldn't affect this.

alex: Pinged. Quick theory: stream first byte is fine but last-chunk stalls due to coalescing/backpressure in upstream worker threads. Seen similar once when bursty KV cache miss caused longer generation for last tokens.

emma-ml: Do we have model-level logs for those request IDs? If it's last-token compute, we'd see high per-token latency. If it's flush, we'd see chunks sitting in the TCP buffer.

jason-support: Customer logs attached (trimmed):

```
request_id: req-ACME-337
mode: streaming
client_path: browser-sse
events: [first_chunk=150ms, subsequent_chunks=20-40ms, final_chunk=12s]
```

alex: That final_chunk=12s is the interesting one. Can someone run tcpdump/ss on the edge for the request ID window? If packets are sent but client not getting them, it's network. If packets are sent late, it's our app.

ryan-eng: Running tcpdump on edge node 10.4.2.11 now for that timespan. Also checking our upstream queue metrics. Quick note: we recently enabled "stream_coalesce=true" flag in edge for latency smoothing. Could be interacting badly with h2 multiplexing.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-02-20T18:02:17Z: rolled feature flag stream_coalesce=true to 60% of edge nodes.

maria: Aha — rollout timing matches customer reports (started ~18:05). Please treat as suspected cause until proven otherwise.

emma-ml: I'll pull model runtime traces for the request IDs. Alex/ryan — can you check flush timings in proxy logs (we log flush events with reason: timer vs buffer_full vs connection_idle)?

alex: Got proxy logs for req-ACME-337 (sanitized):

```
[18:06:03.112] recv first_chunk
[18:06:03.130] flush chunk (timer)
[18:06:03.150] chunk sent
[18:06:03.170] subsequent chunks sent
[18:06:03.182] generation complete
[18:06:15.190] flush final_chunk (coalesce-window)
[18:06:15.192] final_chunk sent
```

alex: So generation completed at 18:06:03.182 but final_chunk wasn't flushed until 12s later due to a coalesce-window flush timeout. That matches customer "final chunk stall".

jason-support: Customer shows client saw nothing after 1st few chunks until ~18:06:15. They're pretty upset.

maria: Action plan: 1) roll back stream_coalesce flag to reduce tails immediately; 2) add short-term route override for heavy AcmeCorp tenant to non-coalescing edge nodes; 3) postmortem + telemetry to measure impact. Alex/Ryan can you execute 1 and 2? Emma, grab runtime traces.

ryan-eng: Rolling back stream_coalesce on the edge pool now (targeted rollback w/ canary). Patch posted: 

```
edge-config set stream_coalesce=false --target=canary-pool
```

deploy-bot: rollback action 1788882030: stream_coalesce=false applied to canary-pool.

ryan-eng: Also adding a tenant-specific routing override for AcmeCorp to avoid nodes that had the flag earlier.

alex: After rollback I see flush events realigning — new sample (same test after rollback):

```
[18:12:05.012] recv first_chunk
[18:12:05.030] flush chunk (timer)
[18:12:05.052] chunk sent
[18:12:05.062] generation complete
[18:12:05.064] flush final_chunk (immediate)
[18:12:05.065] final_chunk sent
```

alex: Total latency now ~60-80ms. Appears rollout flag was the smoking gun.

emma-ml: Runtime traces show no per-token tail processing. Model finished quickly. No inference regression.

maria: Great. Can we ship a follow-up: make coalesce-window configurable per-tenant and add telemetry that records coalesce-induced delays > 1s (so we can alert)? Also ensure flag rollouts are gradual with synthetic streaming tests against canary tenants.

alex: Agreed. I'll file ENG-RUNTIME ticket and add a metric: streaming.coalesce.delay.p99_by_tenant.

jason-support: Communicated back to customer: immediate rollback done, we routed them to safe nodes, and we're doing follow-up engineering changes. They're ok for now but want a timeline.

maria: Assign owners + ETA: Alex (engineer) - ticket + metric (ETA 3d). Ryan (infra) - add tenant routing override API + safety checks (ETA 2d). Emma (ml) - confirm no model changes and add regression test (ETA 2d). I'll draft an incident summary and customer-facing note.

sre-oncall: Added monitoring alert: if streaming.coalesce.delay.p99_by_region > 500ms for 5m -> pager.

jason-support: Customer accepted interim explanation and asked for a postmortem. I'll keep thread updated when they reopen. :white_check_mark:

maria: Closing loop — we'll publish a short postmortem and follow-up config controls. Thanks team.

sre-oncall: Note: consider adding a synthetic client that exercises SSE/h2 streaming during feature rollouts to catch this automatically.
